rationale: Edge-case lens ran clean; acceptance was genuine no-spec (no story/spec artifact, never dispatched) which floors confidence at low. 2.3 reachability checks dismissed 3 edge-case candidates as noise (unquoted-UninstallString split confirmed false via tauri-bundler's own quoting, HKLM/HKCU hive mismatch confirmed impossible since installMode has always been currentUser, manifest-cache race is a trivial needless-refetch). 1 finding (installer download/host/artifact verification) is deferred: the original task explicitly scopes it out ("no artifact verification (deferred, leave a comment marking the hook point)") and the code already carries that marker comment — see code-review-deferred.md. 4 blocking patch findings remain: commit-format violation on all 5 commits (standards, fail), NSIS uninstall exit code ignored, lost error logging on manifest-fetch failure, and undetected silent-installer launch failure before app exit.

standards_review.notes: git-workflow.md requires `<type>: <desc>` (feat|fix|docs|test|chore|refactor); all 5 commits use `EPMCDME-15055: <desc>` instead - none carry a recognized type prefix.
no .ai-run/guides/standards/code-quality.md in the repo and no code_quality ArtifactRef was passed
no .ai-run/guides/development/security-patterns.md in the repo and no security ArtifactRef was passed; a concrete security issue was found anyway and is reported in blocking_findings

findings.title: Commit subjects lack required type prefix
findings.problem: All 5 commits in range use `EPMCDME-15055: <description>` instead of git-workflow.md's required `<type>: <short description>` format (type in feat|fix|docs|test|chore|refactor).
findings.impact: Violates the documented, blocking commit-format standard; breaks tooling/changelog generation that depends on conventional commit types.
findings.recommendation: Reword the commit subjects (or the squashed MR commit) to lead with a documented type, e.g. 'feat: spawn Windows installer silently with /S', keeping the EPMCDME-15055 reference in the body.

findings.title: Prior-version uninstall exit code ignored
findings.problem: NSIS_HOOK_PREINSTALL reads the prior version's UninstallString and runs `ExecWait '$0 /S'` but never captures or checks the resulting exit code.
findings.impact: If the prior silent uninstall fails or hangs (locked files, permission denied), the new install proceeds over a failed/partial uninstall, corrupting install state.
findings.recommendation: Capture the ExecWait return value (e.g. `ExecWait '$0 /S' $1`) and Abort or surface a warning when it is non-zero.

findings.title: Manifest-fetch failures no longer logged
findings.problem: check_for_update's error arm now discards the error entirely (`Err(_e) => { ... }`, no eprintln), so invalid-manifest and network/parse failures are indistinguishable and unrecorded.
findings.impact: Update-check failures in the field can no longer be diagnosed from logs.
findings.recommendation: Log `_e` (e.g. `eprintln!("[app-updater] update check failed: {e}")`) before discarding it.

findings.title: Silent installer launch failure undetected before app exit
findings.problem: launch_installer spawns the installer with /S (fire-and-forget via Command::spawn) and download_and_install sleeps 500ms then unconditionally calls app.exit(0), with no check that the spawned process is still running or exited non-zero.
findings.impact: If the silent installer fails immediately after spawn (corrupt exe, missing dependency, permission issue), the app has already exited with no new version installed and no visible error to the user.
findings.recommendation: After the wait, use try_wait() on the spawned child (Command::spawn's Child handle) to check for an early non-zero exit and report failure instead of blindly exiting.
